To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the introduction of anionic surfactants in the multilayer assemblies based on poly(alkylenimine) containing an osmyl complex and glucose oxidase allows a sensitive increase in the polyelectroyte and enzyme uptake, enhancing its catalysis in the presence of the substrate glucose.

the introduction of surfactant in layer-by-layer assembled films based on OsPA and GOx allows the sensitive increase of the enzyme uptake at physiological pH and the enhancement of its catalytic behavior, but the meso-structural organization of the ternary system is also influenced by the length of the surfactants alkyl chain, which in turn affects the electron transfer properties.

hydrophobic interactions between surfactants and the polyallylamine backbone can be used as an additional variable for controlling the meso-structure and the bioelectrochemical performance of the multilayers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bioactive interfaces with accurate control of the supr...

the development of a new approach that allows the rational control of the suprastructure of bioelectrocatalytically active interfaces, which can be tuned by a combination of electrostatic and hydrophobic forces.
the development of new strategies for the construction of multilayered bioelectrodes with improved electrocatalytic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the interplay between hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions in the ternary multicomposite system leads to a complex interrelation between meso-organization, enzyme coverage, bioelectrocatalysis, and hydrophobic properties of the bioelectrode.
the interplay between the hydrophilic and hydrophobic properties of the multilayers, which are strongly affected by the surfactant nature, determines the bioelectrocatalysis of the ternary system.
the interplay between the hydrophobic interactions and the electrostatic interactions between the different components of the multilayers is crucial for the construction of a functional interface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the introduction of a surfactant into the layer-by-layer system can be exploited to tune the hydrophobic properties of the whole assembly, and this in turn allows a better control over the enzyme coverage and the electron transfer properties of the bioelectrochemical interface.
the hydrophobic interactions between the surfactant and the OsPA/GOx complex are responsible for the formation of mesoscale domains within the multilayer film.
the incorporation of anionic surfactants in layer-by-layer films is a promising tool to modulate the supramolecular assembly of the multilayers and the functional properties of bioactive interfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the incorporation of hydrophobic components into the multilayer system is an efficient way to control the supramolecular organization of the composite film, and therefore its bioelectrocatalytical properties.
a fine-tuning of the supramolecule architecture and the incorporation of hydrophobic interactions can provide an efficient way to control the functional properties of multilayered assemblies.

the interplay between the different forces involved in the formation of the multilayers (ionic, hydrophobic, and steric) can be exploited as a tool to tune the supramolecular structure and functional properties of the resulting bioelectrocatalytically active interfaces.
